classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that equal distances at different speeds take unequal times, introduce a convenient common distance despite none being given, and calculate total distance divided by total time.

content.prompt: My average walking speed up a mountain was 3 km/h. I then ran down the same mountain at a speed of 12 km/h. What was my average speed for the entire trip up and down the mountain?

answer.short:
$4.8\text{ km/h}$

Divide the total distance by the total time for both legs.
answer.worked:
Take the one-way distance as $12\text{ km}$; any equal distance for both legs gives the same average speed.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Time uphill}&=12\div3=4\text{ h}\\\text{Time downhill}&=12\div12=1\text{ h}\\\text{Total distance}&=12+12=24\text{ km}\\\text{Total time}&=4+1=5\text{ h}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{24}{5}\text{ km/h}\\\text{Average speed}&=4.8\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$
